name: Minesweeper
miniText: What can local numerical clues reveal about hidden global arrangements? NetLogo Minesweeper hides mines on a grid, reveals neighboring mine counts after safe clicks, and expands empty regions automatically. Winning requires uncovering every safe square; a mine click ends the game. Kaye [1] establishes the computational difficulty of a formal consistency problem, Golan [2] studies graph structure and tractable cases, and Jaynes [3] supplies probabilistic reasoning when clues do not determine a unique safe action. The interactive baseline illustrates constraints, partial information, and the distinction between deduction and risk. Its fixed board generation, finite size, and neighborhood definition matter. Worst-case complexity theorems concern generalized problem families, not the difficulty of each displayed board. The game is a computational illustration and provides no model of physical mine detection or humanitarian clearance performance.
